description: Build a complete simple authentication system (signup, login, logout) without email verification. Uses JSON file storage for users, bcryptjs for password hashing, jose for JWT session tokens stored in cookies, and proxy.ts for route protection.
steps: Install dependencies: jose, bcryptjs, @types/bcryptjs, server-only, zod using bun add
Create app/lib/definitions.ts with Zod schemas for signup (username + password, no email) and login forms, and TypeScript types for User and SessionPayload

Create app/lib/db.ts - a simple JSON-file-based user store at data/users.json. Provide functions: getUserByUsername(username), createUser(username, hashedPassword), getUserById(id). Use fs/promises for read/write with proper locking.

Create app/lib/session.ts - session management using jose (HS256 JWT). Functions: encrypt(payload), decrypt(token), createSession(userId), updateSession(), deleteSession(). Store session as httpOnly cookie named 'session'. Use process.env.SESSION_SECRET (generate a default for dev). Import 'server-only'.

Create app/actions/auth.ts - Server Actions for signup, login, logout. signup: validate with Zod, check duplicate username, hash password with bcryptjs, create user in db, create session, redirect to /dashboard. login: validate, find user, compare password, create session, redirect to /dashboard. logout: delete session, redirect to /login. Use 'use server' directive.

Create app/signup/page.tsx - Client Component signup form with username and password fields. Use useActionState for form validation feedback. Style with responsive Tailwind CSS, use semantic HTML (main, section, form, label elements).

Create app/login/page.tsx - Client Component login form with username and password fields. Use useActionState for form validation feedback. Style with responsive Tailwind CSS, use semantic HTML. Include link to signup page.

Create app/dashboard/page.tsx - Protected Server Component page. Import verifySession from DAL, display welcome message with username, include logout button (form with logout action). Style with responsive Tailwind, semantic HTML.

Create app/lib/dal.ts - Data Access Layer with verifySession() function that checks the session cookie, decrypts it, and redirects to /login if invalid. Also getUser() to fetch current user data. Import 'server-only', use React cache().

Create proxy.ts in the project root - protect /dashboard route (redirect to /login if no valid session). Redirect authenticated users away from /login and /signup to /dashboard. Use the Next.js 16 proxy convention (export function proxy, export config with matcher).
Create a .env.local file with SESSION_SECRET set to a randomly generated base64 string for development
Update app/page.tsx - replace the default Next.js landing with a simple home page that links to /login and /signup. Use semantic HTML and Tailwind CSS.
Create data/ directory with an empty users.json file initialized as an empty array []
acceptance_criteria: bun run build completes without errors
bun run lint passes without errors
Signup page at /signup accepts username and password (no email), validates input, creates user, and redirects to /dashboard
Login page at /login accepts username and password, authenticates user, and redirects to /dashboard
Dashboard page at /dashboard is protected - unauthenticated users are redirected to /login
Logout from dashboard clears session and redirects to /login
proxy.ts properly redirects unauthenticated users from /dashboard to /login
proxy.ts redirects authenticated users from /login and /signup to /dashboard
All pages use semantic HTML elements (main, section, nav, header, form, label) and responsive Tailwind CSS classes
No email verification is required anywhere in the flow
verification: Run 'bun run build' and confirm it succeeds with exit code 0
Run 'bun run lint' and confirm it passes
findings: Build uses Turbopack and shows worker_threads NotImplementedError warnings (bun limitation) but compiles successfully. proxy.ts must NOT import from app/lib/session.ts directly because session.ts imports server-only which would fail in the proxy context - instead, duplicated the decrypt logic inline in proxy.ts using jose directly. Zod 4 uses { error: 'msg' } syntax for custom errors. The .env.local file is not committed (gitignored by default in Next.js).
